rules.architecture: higher mean CV macro-F1 over the 3 splits; if the difference < mean fold SD: lower mean CV gap if the gap difference >= 0.01, else fewer parameters
rules.split: among splits with mean CV macro-F1 within one fold SD (of the best split) of the best: the largest training portion
rules.activation: the activation used in the CV of that (architecture, split)
rules.best_activation_overall: declared only if |mean paired Stage G delta macro-F1| >= 0.02 AND the winner takes >= 11 of 15 pairs; else no winner
rules.best_generalisation: lowest mean Stage G train-val gap among architectures with mean val F1 within 0.05 of the best; also reported for CV
rules.best_efficiency: lowest GPU batch-1 latency among architectures with mean Stage G val F1 within 0.02 of the best
caveats: CV used one activation per split
split choice is confounded with training-set size
CV nested test sets are not independent
only EfficientNetB0 and DenseNet121 have CV evidence

final_model.why_architecture: F1 difference 0.0158 < fold SD 0.0159 (tie); lower generalisation gap decides (-0.0215)
final_model.why_split: splits within one SD of the best: ['70_30', '80_20', '90_10']; largest training portion chosen
